title: You Can't Outrun a Bear Market, but Successful Investors Don't Have to Because They Follow This Playbook Instead
detail:
You Can't Outrun a Bear Market, but Successful Investors Don't Have to Because They Follow This Playbook Instead
Jack Delaney, The Motley Fool
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 11:11 AM PDT 4 min read
^GSPC
NVDA
Trade NVIDIA on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) has been humming along in 2026, up 14% as of Oct. 13. Still, investors may feel like they have to keep looking over their shoulders, as inflation remains stubborn, U.S. families falling behind on loan obligations are at their highest levels since 2010, and U.S. debt levels sit above $40 trillion.

That's why, despite this year's rally, some may be worried about a pullback deep enough to trigger a bear market, defined as a drop of 20% or more from a recent high. There's no way to outrun a bear market; if one is going to happen, it will.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Still, successful investors know the playbook that helps them avoid costly mistakes when stocks seem to be doing nothing but heading lower.

Image source: Getty Images.
The cost of selling during a bear market

When stock prices are dropping, it's easy to feel that selling is better than doing nothing. After all, it only feels natural to protect what you have left rather than watch the value of your investment decrease even further.

What history suggests, however, is that panic selling can be a costly mistake.

It sounds counterintuitive to a natural perception of how stocks perform, but some of the best days for the S&P 500 came during a bear market. From 1996 through 2025, 48% of the best days for the S&P 500 happened during a bear market, according to Hartford Funds. That was followed by 28% of the best days occurring during the first two months of a bull market, and 24% during the rest of the bull market. And the cost of missing those best days is jarring.

A $10,000 investment in the S&P 500 in 1996 would have been worth $192,167 by the end of 2025. Missing just the 10 best days, however, would have lowered that investment by 56% to $85,490. It gets even worse from there, as missing the 20 best days would have yielded a $49,551 return, and missing the 30 best days would have turned that $10,000 investment into just $31,123.

The investing game plan

Wanting to sell during a market downturn is natural. The good news is that the selling itch doesn't have to make the decisions.

Instead, a portfolio already filled with high-conviction stocks can help mitigate the risk of knee-jerk reactions. A portfolio filled with mostly speculative positions can be hit hard when the market faces a downturn and is more likely to cause panic selling. Successful investors fill their portfolios with stocks that they are comfortable buying more of if prices drop.

title: What Changed In eBay's Story?
detail:
What Changed In eBay's Story?
Trefis Team

^GSPC
AMZN
WMT
MELI
Explore stocks on Coinbase

Image from Pixabay

Investors are paying a premium for eBay (EBAY). The stock currently trades at 4.3 times its sales over the past twelve months, compared to 3.1 for the S&P 500. Justifying that valuation requires tracking a recent shift in corporate messaging. Back in April 2025, during the fiscal Q1 2025 call, management emphasized the uncertainty that tariffs and trade policy changes created for eBay's sellers and buyers. That rhetoric has faded. So what has management been talking up instead?

eBay Now Talks Up eBay Live And Depop

During the fiscal Q2 2026 call on August 5, 2026, management talked up eBay Live, which posted another record quarter. Gross merchandise volume on eBay Live, the value of goods sold through it, grew roughly eightfold, management said. Furthermore, management believes the platform is gaining share across all 7 markets where it operates.

Management also said eBay had completed its acquisition of Depop the week before. This deal broadens eBay's fashion portfolio and expands its reach, management noted. On the same call, management talked up using AI to change how people buy and sell on eBay.

Management no longer emphasizing trade policy marks a recent departure. As late as the fiscal Q1 2026 call on April 29, 2026, management described shipping as a major focus for the year amid an increasingly complex trade policy landscape.

Shifts like this test every retirement plan. If your advisor recently retired, it is a good moment for a free second opinion from our partner firm.

eBay's Sales Have Sped Up Over The Past Year

Financial performance has accelerated over the past year. eBay's revenue grew 14.8% in the April to June 2026 quarter, up from 6.1% in the same quarter a year earlier. The operating margin rose to 21.6% in that quarter, compared to 17.5% a year earlier, so operating profit grew faster than revenue.

Certain segments within the marketplace expanded faster than the broader business. Gross merchandise volume across eBay grew 14% from a year earlier in fiscal Q2 2026, excluding currency moves, management said. Meanwhile, consumer-to-consumer trade, recommerce (the resale of used goods), and the categories eBay has chosen to focus on each grew more than 20%.

Should eBay Holders Worry Less About Tariffs Now?

For a holder, the quieter tone is a modest positive. Management did not raise trade policy on the latest call, though it called the trade landscape increasingly complex as recently as April. Beyond the rhetoric, eBay's sales growth and operating margin were both higher in the latest quarter than a year earlier. Shareholders have benefited over the past year as well. The stock returned 32.5%, compared to 17.3% for the S&P 500.

title: Is Boston Scientific Stock Riskier Than It Was A Year Ago?
detail:
Is Boston Scientific Stock Riskier Than It Was A Year Ago?
Trefis Team
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 12:18 PM PDT 3 min read
BSX
^GSPC
MDT
ABT
JNJ
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Unsplash

Investors in Boston Scientific (BSX) hold stakes in a medical device maker that grew revenue 13.5% over the twelve months to June 2026. Yet the shares have lost 54.7% over the past year, trailing a 17.3% gain for the S&P 500. In August, a cyberattack disrupted the company's manufacturing and order shipments. So has the risk in holding Boston Scientific shares gone up or down over the past year?

Riskier: Capital Spending Is Now Above Research Spending

The risk has indeed increased, and the evidence appears in how Boston Scientific spends its cash. Over the twelve months to June 2026, capital spending reached $2.72 billion. This outlay exceeded the $2.15 billion allocated to research over the same months. Prior to this, research spending had been the larger of the two at every quarter end since at least September 2011, a streak of 59 in a row.

The higher capital spending left the company with less free cash flow. Over the twelve months to June 2026, free cash flow totaled $1.81 billion, down from $3.18 billion a year earlier. Debt rose modestly during the same period: total debt stood at $12.6 billion at the end of June 2026, compared with $12.0 billion a year earlier.

Most Of The Extra Spending Came In One Quarter

Boston Scientific's capital spending in April to June 2026 reached $1.93 billion, compared with $245 million in the same quarter a year earlier. Capital spending in that one quarter alone was larger than in the whole twelve months to June 2025.

The underlying business kept growing through that quarter. Revenue rose 7.5% from a year earlier, and operating margin widened to 22.9%, up from 18.6% a year earlier. Cash from operations over the twelve months to June 2026 also increased, reaching $4.53 billion from $4.29 billion. So the drop in free cash flow came from what Boston Scientific spent, not from what it earned.

A Thinner Cushion For A Bad Quarter

For shareholders, the existing debt still looks manageable, but the company now generates less spare cash to absorb a bad quarter. Operating income over the twelve months to June 2026 covered interest expense 12.1 times. Yet free cash flow in April to June 2026 was negative $451 million, compared with a positive $1.04 billion a year earlier.

The broader outlook has weakened as well. On July 29, management lowered its 2026 revenue growth forecast to 6.0% at the midpoint, down from 7.8% in its April release. In September, the company said the cyberattack was likely to have a material impact on its third-quarter and full-year 2026 results. The company's next report, expected on or around October 28, 2026, will cover the quarter the attack hit.

title: Update: US Equity Indexes Mixed After Hot Producer Price Inflation Print, Tech Declines Accompany Sliding Treasury Yields
detail:
PREMIUM
Update: US Equity Indexes Mixed After Hot Producer Price Inflation Print, Tech Declines Accompany Sliding Treasury Yields
MT Newswires
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 10:46 AM PDT 3 min read
^GSPC
^DJI
^IXIC

(Updates with index/price moves, macroeconomic data, and company/geopolitical news from the first paragraph.)

US equity indexes traded mixed as a rotation out of technology stocks coincided with both a slump in government bond yields and gains in defensive names, following the release of producer price inflation and retail sales.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.2% to 26,640.1, while the S&P 500 rose 0.2% to 7,733.5 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 1% to 52,114.9 after midday Thursday. Healthcare, materials, and financials topped the gainers.

US producer prices jumped at the fastest pace in more than four years in September, driven by a surge in energy costs. Energy was the steepest decliner.

The producer price index rose 1.3% last month from 0.5% in August, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said. The print marked the strongest pace of advance since March 2022, and is more than double the 0.6% climb projected in a Bloomberg-compiled survey.

Annually, the PPI climbed 6.3%, the biggest jump since December 2022 and exceeding the 5.4% estimate. August was revised to a 5.6% gain from 5.4%.

US retail sales rose 0.8% in September, above the 0.3% gain expected in a Bloomberg-compiled survey and August's revised 1.3% gain, according to the US Commerce Department. A 6.4% jump in nominal gasoline spending drove most of the sales growth, Jefferies said in a note.

Control group sales rose 0.1% after a 1.2% increase in August, the Jefferies note said. "This was the result of modest increases and declines across the various sub-categories."

Most US Treasury yields declined, with the two-year down 4.7 basis points to 4.76%. The 10-year yield sank 10.5 basis points to 5.09%, and the 30-year rate plunged 10.4 basis points to 5.42%.

Gold futures jumped 1.5% to $4,168.10, and silver futures advanced 2.2% to $57.12.

The cost of protecting CoreWeave's (CRWV) debt against default for five years rose Thursday by as much as 74.5 basis points to 1194.5 basis points, an intraday record, with swaps pricing in a chance of default at over 60% within the next five years, Bloomberg reported Thursday, citing data from ICE Data Services.

The PHLX Semiconductor slumped 2.2% in its seventh consecutive day of losses.

Nine of the bottom 10 were technology names among stocks with market capitalization exceeding $200 billion, according to data compiled by Finviz. Dell Technologies (DELL) led decliners for a second day, down 8.3%.

Ukraine will resume strikes on Russia's oil refineries after halting attacks for three days following a surprise "energy ceasefire," CNN reported, citing President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Meanwhile, two cargo ships have sunk near the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours after being struck by unknown projectiles in separate incidents, CNN reported, citing the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore and the International Maritime Organization.

The International Energy Agency agreed to complete the remaining releases of about 100 million barrels of oil, consistent with the March collective action in response to the Hormuz crisis. The IEA said it will accelerate the remaining releases, including more than 20 million barrels of diesel as soon as possible.

The front-month US West Texas Intermediate crude oil contract surged 3% to $97.93 per barrel, while global benchmark Brent was 0.2% lower at $105.87 per barrel.

title: Do Altria's Dividends Make Up For A Lagging Stock?
detail:
Do Altria's Dividends Make Up For A Lagging Stock?
Trefis Team
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 11:28 AM PDT 3 min read
MO
^GSPC
SPGI
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Selling Marlboro cigarettes and nicotine pouches generates the cash Altria Group (MO) uses to pay its dividend. Over the past year, those dividends added about 7.6 percentage points to the stock's return. Yet over a five-year timeline, the share price rose less than the S&P 500. Take a guess: once every dividend is counted, did a five-year Altria holder end up ahead of the market or behind it?

How Far Has Altria Stock Trailed The Market?

Investors tracking price appreciation alone from October 6, 2021, to October 14, 2026, would conclude that Altria stock trailed the S&P 500 by 19.6 percentage points. The shares gained 57.4% during that period, while the S&P 500 climbed 77.0%. A simple glance at a stock chart points to an underperforming asset.

Dividends like this test every retirement plan. If your advisor recently retired, it is a good moment for a free second opinion from our partner firm.

How Much Did Altria's Dividends Add?

Factoring in payouts changes the calculation. Reinvesting those dividends added 73.8 percentage points to the five-year return. This brought the return on Altria stock to 131.2% over those years. Dividends, not the share price, generated more than half of what an Altria holder earned.

Did The Dividends Close The Gap For Altria Holders?

Altria more than closed the performance gap. This holds even after factoring in the broader market's dividends, as the table illustrates.

Return from Oct 6, 2021 to Oct 14, 2026

With dividends included, the S&P 500 returned 88.7% over the same five years. That leaves Altria 42.5 percentage points ahead. The cash paid out by the company turned a stock that trailed the market on price into one that beat it.

That advantage disappears over a longer time horizon. Over ten years, the S&P 500 with dividends beat Altria with dividends by 189.9 percentage points.

What This Means If You Own Altria For Income

Income investors rely on dividends to generate the bulk of their returns in Altria, accepting modest share price growth in the process. S&P 500 dividends added just under one percentage point to the index return over the past year, far less than Altria dividends did. Over five years, that stream of cash more than made up for the slower share price.

The cash comes from tobacco. Most of Altria's sales come from smokeable products. Net revenues for those items, which include excise taxes, fell 3.4% in fiscal 2025.

Tracking the stock's return with dividends alongside the S&P 500 offers a clearer picture for income holders than looking at the dividend in isolation.
